name: Giant herbs — alocasia, taro, bananas and their kin
status: 8 archetypal species (full list archived in docs/plant_archive)
notes: The big soft-stemmed plants of wet tropical gaps, stream banks and camp edges: elephant ears (Alocasia, Colocasia, Xanthosoma) with metre-wide leaves, and the banana family (wild Musa, Ensete, the traveller's palm, heliconia, torch ginger). None are trees: a stem grows in one season, flowers once and dies, and the clump lives on through suckers, so growth stages run in weeks and a cleared patch is waist-deep in them by the next season — they are the pioneers of gaps and landslides. Bat- and bird-pollinated. Taro, cocoyam, banana and the cultivated elephant ears are camp-followers and the staple roots and fruit of tropical camps; big leaves are roofing and wrapping.

repro.note: giant herbs, not trees: each stem grows in a season, fruits or flowers once and dies, replaced by suckers from the clump — fast growth stages, visible in weeks

canopy.source: New Guinea highland forest. Largest herb on Earth; 15 m stems. Kew POWO.
